approachQuestion.prompt:
Find the first completed row

Input: nonempty rows of integer labels and an array draws. Each label occurs at most once across all rows. A draw marks its label if that label is on the board; repeating a draw has no additional effect. Return the earliest zero-based draw index after which some row has all its labels marked, or −1 if no row completes.

Example 1: rows = [[7,2],[9]], draws = [7,7,4,2,9]. Output: 3. Example 2: rows = [[5]], draws = [3,5]. Output: 1. Example 3: rows = [[5]], draws = []. Output: −1. There are between 1 and 200,000 rows, each nonempty; total board entries N ≤ 200,000 and number of draws d ≤ 200,000.

Constraints: input is immutable; all identifiers and numeric entries are signed 32-bit integers unless specified. Arithmetic uses signed 64-bit integers. Prefer the least expected running-time growth, then avoid unnecessary asymptotic auxiliary storage. Non-adversarial hashing of fixed-size integer keys/tuples has expected amortized constant cost.

options.text: Map each board label to its row and an unmarked flag; initialize a remaining count for each row. Process draws in order, decrementing the affected row only for a first mark, and return when its count reaches zero.
options.feedback: The inverse index locates the only affected row, and the mark flag prevents duplicate draws from consuming the same entry twice.

options.text: Build a map of board labels to marked flags. After every draw, scan every row to check whether all its labels are marked.
options.feedback: This keeps marking correct but repeatedly rechecks unchanged rows. Per-row remaining counts remove that work.

options.text: Map labels to rows and decrement a row count on every matching draw, including repeated draws.
options.feedback: rows [[7,2]] and draws [7,7] would falsely complete the row while 2 is still unmarked.

options.text: Count all matching draws globally and return once that count reaches the length of the shortest row.
options.feedback: rows [[1,2],[3,4]], draws [1,3] mark two entries in different rows; no row is complete.

feedback.reason: Use an inverse index to update only the affected aggregate, and make repeated events idempotent.
details: Build a label-to-(row,marked) map and remaining-count array. Process draws from the start; ignore absent labels and already-marked entries. Otherwise mark once, decrement that row’s remaining count, and return the draw index if it becomes zero. Return −1 if draws end.

Repeated draws must not decrement a row twice. The inverse index identifies the affected row, and its marked flag makes repeated events idempotent. Return at the first transition to zero remaining entries.

Process draws in order, decrementing the affected row only for a first mark, and return when its count reaches zero.”: The inverse index locates the only affected row, and the mark flag prevents duplicate draws from consuming the same entry twice.

“Build a map of board labels to marked flags. After every draw, scan every row to check whether all its labels are marked.”: This keeps marking correct but repeatedly rechecks unchanged rows. Per-row remaining counts remove that work.
“Map labels to rows and decrement a row count on every matching draw, including repeated draws.”: rows [[7,2]] and draws [7,7] would falsely complete the row while 2 is still unmarked.
“Count all matching draws globally and return once that count reaches the length of the shortest row.”: rows [[1,2],[3,4]], draws [1,3] mark two entries in different rows; no row is complete.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Find the first completed row — analyzed method”, N is total board entries and d is the number of draws. Preprocessing is included; the bound is for the worst legal draw order. Choose its time and auxiliary-space pair. Use the tightest standard bound for the worst legal input for the stated size parameters, with expected time over non-adversarial hashing. Fixed-width integer and fixed-size tuple hash operations take expected amortized O(1); arithmetic, comparison and copying one integer take O(1). Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input and returned result, includes all maps, sets, temporary copies and call stacks. The method is iterative, with constant call-stack space.

feedback.reason: Build the board index once and update at most one row per draw.
details: Use an inverse index to update only the affected aggregate, and make repeated events idempotent.

Constructing the inverse index costs expected O(N). At most d draws each perform expected constant-cost lookup and one count update, so worst-input expected O(N+d+1). Early completion can shorten the draw scan.
The inverse map contains N board entries; the count array has at most N rows because every row is nonempty. Flags live in those entries, including no state for unrelated draws. Thus O(N+1).
“Expected O(N + d + 1) worst-input time; O(N + 1) auxiliary space.”: Correct under the stated expected/amortized hashing model.
“Expected O(Nd + 1) time; O(N + 1) space.”: No full board scan follows a draw; each draw updates at most one row.
“Expected O(N + d + 1) time; O(d + 1) auxiliary space as the tight bound.”: The inverse board index is built from N entries even when d is zero.
“Expected O(d + 1) time independent of N; O(1) space.”: Building the board index and remaining counts requires preprocessing and retained state.
